h1: The 5 Best Murphy Beds With Storage and Desks of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Murphy Beds With Desk: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: five Murphy beds with fold-down desks and storage, compared on size, weight rating, shelving, charging and installation.
mainKeyword: best murphy bed with storage and desk
summary: The Merax Queen is the best overall, with a fold-down desk with lights, a built-in outlet, shelves and drawers. The Softa Queen has the highest stated weight rating at 1200 lb. The KEIKI uses gas struts for easy folding, the MERITLINE Full is the compact option with bookcase shelves, and the LUXOAK is a no-desk budget cabinet.
intro: A Murphy bed with a built-in desk promises two rooms in one, but the useful question is what the desk does when the bed is down. On most combination units the desk folds out only while the bed is stored, so you work during the day and sleep at night, never both at once. Buyers often find that out after assembly, when the cabinet is already on the wall.

Our editors reviewed five beds from their listings and ranked them on how completely each handles bed, workspace and storage. Weight ratings, mechanism, lighting and charging all fed the Primea score. Several figures are the seller's own claims, which we flag, and one listing did not confirm its price, so we leave its cost out.

products.name: Merax Queen Size Murphy Bed with Desk and Lights, Power Outlet, Open Storage Shelves and Drawers
products.verdict: The most complete bed-desk-storage combination in the group.
products.description:
The Merax Queen is the most complete bed-desk-storage unit here. A fold-down desk comes with built-in lights, a power outlet sits in the cabinet so a laptop and lamp have somewhere to plug in, and open shelves and drawers hold books and clothes. The platform is queen size, in an antique white finish, and it sits in the $500 and up bucket.

It wins because it covers the whole shopping list: desk, lighting, power and storage. The Softa claims a higher weight rating but lists a charging station without a lit desk.

Buy it for a small apartment that needs bed, workspace and storage in one wall. The caveats are likely professional installation, since the cabinet is large and heavy, and the highest price bucket in the guide.
products.idealFor: Small apartments that need a bed, desk and storage in one wall.
products.skipIf: You cannot handle a large assembly.

products.name: Softa Queen Murphy Bed Cabinet with Storage Drawer, Charging Station, 1200 LBS Heavy Duty Wood Wall Bed with Fold-Down Desk
products.verdict: A fold-down desk, drawer and charging with a 1200 lb stated rating.
products.description:
The Softa Queen is a cabinet bed with a fold-down desk, a storage drawer, a charging station and a stated 1200 lb heavy duty rating. No box spring is needed. Charging at the desk saves a trip to the wall for phones and tablets.

It ranks just below the Merax because it lacks a lit desk and open shelving, though the stated weight rating is the highest here. The rating is useful if two adults use the bed nightly, but it is the seller's claim, not a lab figure.

Buy it for couples who want a high stated limit. Skip it if you want open shelving for books. The caveat: a 1200 lb rating does not tell you how the desk or the wall mount behave, so ask the seller about anchor hardware before ordering. It sits in the $500 and up bucket.
products.idealFor: Couples who want a high stated weight rating.

products.name: KEIKI Queen Murphy Bed with Desk, Space-Saving Wall Bed Cabinet, Foldable Hidden Bed Frame with Gas Struts
products.verdict: Gas struts make daily folding noticeably lighter work.
products.description:
The KEIKI Queen is a wood cabinet bed with a fold-down desk and a gas strut fold mechanism. Gas struts balance the weight of the mattress and frame so that lifting it is a one-handed job, which matters if you fold the bed away every morning.

It ranks third because the listing says less about storage and charging than the picks above. Its edge is the lift assist, the feature that decides whether a Murphy bed gets used daily or becomes a permanent sleeping platform. It sits in the $500 and up bucket.

Best for someone who will fold the bed every day. The caveats are little storage detail and no charging station listed. If you need shelves and an outlet, step up to the Merax or Softa.
products.idealFor: Daily folders who want effortless lifting.
products.skipIf: You want built-in charging and shelving.

products.name: MERITLINE Full Murphy Bed with Desk and Storage Shelves, Wood Hideaway Murphy Wall Bed with Storage Bookcase
products.verdict: A full-size wood bed with desk and bookcase shelving.
products.description:
The MERITLINE Full is a wood hideaway bed with a fold-down desk and bookcase-style open shelves. A full mattress is about 54 inches wide, which suits one sleeper and leaves more floor in a small combined room than a queen would. The bookcase shelves keep reference books within reach of the desk.

It ranks fourth because a full size gives less room than the queen picks. The bookcase shelves are a plus over the KEIKI, which says little about storage. The listing does not confirm a price bucket, so check the current cost before you decide.

Choose it for a solo sleeper in a studio or spare room. Skip it if two adults will sleep in it. The caveat: with no power or lighting listed, you must plan extension cords or a lamp for the desk.
products.idealFor: Solo sleepers in a small combined room.
products.skipIf: Two adults will sleep in it.

products.name: LUXOAK Full Murphy Cabinet Bed with Storage and Charging Station
products.verdict: Storage and charging at a lower price, with no desk.
products.description:
The LUXOAK Full is a cabinet bed with an integrated storage cabinet and a built-in charging station, in the $200 to $500 bucket. It has no fold-down desk, so it solves the sleeping and storage halves of the problem, not the work half.

It ranks last because the desk is half of this guide's promise. It stays as the lowest-cost route to a space-saving wall bed with practical storage and charging, for a buyer who already owns a desk.

A fit for budget buyers who will keep a separate desk. The caveats are the missing workspace and full size only. If you work from home in the same room, the KEIKI or Merax gives you a surface without buying another table.
products.idealFor: Budget buyers who do not need a desk.

whatMatters.detail: On most combination beds the desk folds down from the cabinet when the bed is stored, which means you cannot use it while the bed is down. That matters if you need to work in the evening or nap in the afternoon. Read the listing for how the desk behaves and what locks in each position. A desk that cannot be used with the bed down limits home-office days.

A stated rating is the load the frame is built to carry, often with a safety margin. A couple plus bedding can approach several hundred pounds. Compare the stated number with your combined weight and check whether it includes the mattress. Remember that the Softa's 1200 lb figure is the seller's own claim.

A full bed is about 54 inches wide and a queen is about 60. The cabinet depth also differs, so measure ceiling height and open-bed projection as well as wall width. Look for exact dimensions in the listing, and mark the footprint on the floor with tape before you decide. The open bed extends far further than the closed cabinet.

Gas struts or springs balance the bed's weight so you can lift it. A weak mechanism makes daily use a chore, and a bed that nobody folds stays open all day. Look for the words gas struts or piston in the title or bullets. The KEIKI names gas struts, and the others do not say.

These beds are heavy and often must be anchored to a wall. Many buyers hire help. Check the listing for assembly notes and anchor hardware, and confirm your wall can take it. A cabinet bed pulled from its anchors is a safety risk, so do not skip the fasteners. Plan for at least two people, and check the wall for studs.

faq.q: Can I use the desk while the bed is down?
faq.a: Usually not. The desk folds out when the bed is stored. Read each listing for how the desk behaves and plan to fold the bed up during work hours. In a studio, that means sleeping and working in shifts.

faq.q: What is the most common mistake?
faq.a: Ignoring room height and depth. Measure the ceiling and the floor space needed when the bed is open, not just the cabinet size. A queen Merax or Softa projects far into the room, so allow clear floor space.

faq.q: Is queen worth it over full?
faq.a: For couples, yes. A solo sleeper in a small room can use a full, such as the MERITLINE, and save floor space. The queen picks cost more and take more room, but they suit a couple far better.

faq.q: Do I need a professional to install it?
faq.a: Many buyers do, because the cabinets are heavy and should anchor to a wall. Check what hardware the listing includes, and ask the seller whether installation is available or recommended for your wall type.

faq.q: Do I need to buy a mattress?
faq.a: Some listings include one, while many do not. Check the mattress thickness limit before choosing one, because a mattress that is too thick will stop the cabinet from closing, or strain the struts.

faq.q: How do I maintain the fold mechanism?
faq.a: Keep the struts clean, check fasteners periodically and avoid loading the desk beyond its stated limit. A rattle in the cabinet usually means a loose bolt, so tighten it before it wears the hole.

finalTake: Buy the Merax if you want every feature in one wall unit, and the Softa if two adults need a high stated rating. The KEIKI suits daily folders, the MERITLINE solo sleepers in small rooms, and the LUXOAK only buyers who already have a desk.
